note: The art plan: plates and scenes to paint, and species canon cannot yet describe. Rendered to docs/art-asks.md and the published plan page by tools/render-art-asks.js.

measured.how: Every tile of the four field maps, asking the game's creatureFor which animal stands there.
measured.note_round2: Plates added on 29 September 2026 for species the owner's lore notes made describable.

plates.name: Dhol
plates.why: Met on 676 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A dhole, the rust-red wild dog of the drove roads: lean, low, with a dark bushy tail, trotting at an even distance beside a dusty track with its ears up, not looking back. A thin string of pack animals is suggested far off in dry plains grass.

plates.name: Shringasaurus
plates.why: Met on 582 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: Shringasaurus, a heavy-bodied, long-necked horned reptile, older than any dinosaur, with a pair of horns curving forward above the eyes like a bull's. It is reared up on its hind legs against a tree, calmly browsing the high leaves, with dry scrub forest below.

plates.name: Tethyan Mud-Snipe
plates.why: Met on 221 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: A mud-snipe, a small mottled brown wading bird with a very long straight bill, probing wet estuary mud at the tide line, a thin sheet of moving water around its feet.

plates.name: Narmada Straight-Tusk
plates.why: Met on 198 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A straight-tusked elephant (Palaeoloxodon), taller than a house roof, with two long pale tusks that run almost straight forward rather than curving out. It is browsing high branches beside a river and has not noticed anyone.

plates.name: Tethyan Reef-Lurker
plates.why: Met on 139 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A murex sea snail with a heavy, spiny, frilled shell in cream and rose, resting in a crevice of a coral reef in clear, sunlit, moving shallow water.

plates.name: Tethyan Blue-Fin Tuna
plates.why: Met on 134 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A bluefin tuna, torpedo-shaped, with a deep blue back and silver flanks, swimming in open sea with two or three of its school behind, sunlight broken through the moving surface above.

plates.name: Tethys Leviathan Calf
plates.why: Met on 134 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A young whale calf, sleek and small, rolling playfully in warm, clear coastal shallows, with just the edge of an adult's great bone-plated flank at the side of the frame.

plates.name: Hammerhead Reef-Shark
plates.why: Met on 133 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A hammerhead shark with its broad, flattened head, gliding low and slow over a pale sandy reef floor, rippling sunlight across the sand.

plates.name: Flying-Fish of the Tethys
plates.why: Met on 130 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A flying fish gliding just above the waves on large, clear, wing-like fins, spray trailing from its tail where it has left a wave crest.

plates.name: Black-Barked Canopy Tendua
plates.why: Met on 124 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A black tendua: a leopard-like cat with a dark coat whose rosettes show only where the light catches, and eyes set forward like a person's. It is lying along a mangrove branch high in the canopy, looking down.

plates.name: Southern Sea-Turtle
plates.why: Met on 124 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A large sea turtle swimming over clear shallows close to a black volcanic beach, flippers mid-stroke, water in motion around it.

plates.name: Tethyan Flying-Squid
plates.why: Met on 123 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A squid that has launched itself out of the sea, gliding over a wave on its spread side-fins with its arms streamlined behind, droplets flying.

plates.name: Reef-dwelling Octopus
plates.why: Met on 122 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: An octopus with bumpy, textured skin in the colours of the coral around it, half-hidden among coral heads in shallow, sunlit water, one arm reaching toward a small crab.

plates.name: Coral-dwelling Moray
plates.why: Met on 120 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A moray eel with a long serpentine body patterned in the red of blood-coral, its head out of a coral crevice, mouth slightly open, in clear moving water.

plates.name: Shattered Sea Barracuda
plates.why: Met on 119 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A barracuda, long, silver and sleek with a jutting lower jaw, holding still in blue water above a coral reef.

plates.name: Southern Sea-Eagle
plates.why: Met on 117 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A large sea eagle with a white head and chest and dark wings, perched on a high cliff edge above the sea, spray rising from the waves below.

plates.name: Southern Reef-Stingray
plates.why: Met on 115 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A sand-coloured stingray lying half-buried in the reef floor, only its eyes, the edge of its disc and its long spined tail showing, ripples of light moving across it.

plates.name: Bone-Plated Orca
plates.why: Met on 110 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: An orca in black and white with thick, pale bony armour plates over its skull and along the ridge of its back, surfacing calmly in open sea with a plume of breath above it.

plates.name: Jungle Hornbill
plates.why: Met on 54 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A large hornbill with a double-pointed casque on its bill, perched in the fork of an old hollow tree with a wild fig held in its bill.

plates.name: Gargoyle-Bat
plates.why: Met on 104 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A bat whose skin is dark and textured like weathered stone, hanging folded from the rocky underside of a floating island among dangling roots, open sky below.

plates.name: Cloud-Lurking Gecko
plates.why: Met on 92 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A pale green gecko with large sticky toe pads, clinging upside down to the underside of a floating rock with a moth nearby, drifting cloud and open sky beneath it.

plates.name: Mangrove Snapping-Turtle
plates.why: Met on 80 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: A snapping turtle with a hooked, sharp beak, half-buried in brackish mud among mangrove roots, only its head and the front of its ridged shell showing.

plates.name: Saraswati Delta Heron
plates.why: Met on 79 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: A tall heron with pale silver-grey feathers standing in estuary shallows with a small bronze-coloured fish in its bill, water rippling around its legs.

plates.name: Lothal Shell-Cracker
plates.why: Met on 77 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: A crab with one hugely oversized, stone-grey crushing claw and one small one, on estuary mud beside a cracked-open mussel shell.

plates.name: Estuary Archer-Fish
plates.why: Met on 72 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: An archer fish at the surface under overhanging mangrove leaves, shooting a thin jet of water up at an insect on a leaf, the jet caught in mid-air.

plates.name: Tethys Pelican
plates.why: Met on 62 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: A pelican with a large bill and a full throat pouch, scooping fish in coastal shallows, water pouring from the pouch.

plates.name: Narmada Cave-Crab
plates.why: Met on 61 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A small, pale, eyeless freshwater crab, almost translucent, on a wet stone in a dark underground stream, lit by one thin shaft of light from above.

plates.name: Plateau Ibex
plates.why: Met on 61 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: An ibex with long, ridged horns sweeping back over its shoulders, standing on a rock ledge no wider than a hand on a cliff face, looking down without concern.

plates.name: Mappa Mundi Forest-Cat
plates.why: Met on 59 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A spotted wildcat with a long balancing tail, walking along a high branch in dense jungle canopy.

plates.name: Narmada Honey-Guide
plates.why: Met on 58 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A small brownish bird with a pale throat on a branch near a cliff, calling and looking back over its shoulder as if to lead, a great golden honeycomb glimpsed on the rock beyond.

plates.name: Banded Scavenger Voay
plates.why: Met on 62 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A voay: a smaller, land-living crocodile standing high on its legs rather than sprawling, with bold dark bands across its back, walking along a forest edge near the sea.

plates.name: Giant Blue-Ringed Octopus
plates.why: Met on 45 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A large octopus, sand-yellow with vivid blue rings across its skin, in a clear rock pool on the reef.

plates.name: Lothal Marsh-Lurker
plates.why: Met on 11 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Dwarka.
plates.subject: A giant river salamander, eight feet long, flat-headed, with wrinkled brown skin and small eyes, lying still in a murky delta pool among reeds with only its head and back above the water.

plates.name: Shattered Sea Oyster
plates.why: Met on 40 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A massive oyster, its rough grey shell open just enough to show an iridescent black pearl, resting on the sea floor in sunlit water.

plates.name: Floating-Island Chameleon
plates.why: Met on 35 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A chameleon whose skin matches the pale green moss around it, hanging by its curled tail from the roots of a mangrove growing off the edge of a floating island, open sky below.

plates.name: Aero-Moth
plates.why: Met on 32 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A large moth with soft, dusty wings patterned like grey clouds, resting on a thorny bramble at the edge of a floating island, sky and far islands behind.

plates.name: Sky-Faring Crab
plates.why: Met on 32 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A pale, light-shelled crab climbing one of the aerial roots that hang from a floating island's mangroves, open sky and cloud below.

plates.name: Cloud-Squirrel
plates.why: Met on 29 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A squirrel mid-leap between two floating rocks, its exceptionally long bushy tail stretched out behind like a rudder, clouds below.

plates.name: Upfalling Elver
plates.why: Met on 29 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A young eel, hand-long and glass-clear, climbing the wet underside of a floating island through rain that is falling upward, droplets rising past it.

plates.name: Lothal Mud-Skipper
plates.why: Met on 28 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: A giant mudskipper, a goggle-eyed fish with a raised back fin, propped on its front fins on a mangrove root above the mud.

plates.name: Lodestone Beetle
plates.why: Met on 27 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A beetle with an iron-dark metallic shell, a few iron filings standing on end against it as if drawn there, on a mineral-streaked stone at the core of a floating island.

plates.name: Estuary Sawfish
plates.why: Met on 25 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A sawfish, a large ray whose snout is a long, flat, toothed saw, gliding low over the brown bed of an estuary, the tip of the saw just breaking the surface.

plates.name: Tendua
plates.why: Met on 21 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A tendua: a spotted, leopard-like cat with eyes set forward like a person's, watching calmly from a reed line at the edge of a wetland.

plates.name: Vindhya Rock-Squirrel
plates.why: Met on 20 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A giant squirrel in rich maroon, cream and orange, sitting at the mouth of its nest hole in a cliff with a pine nut in its paws.
plates.guess: Canon says colourful. The maroon, cream and orange are the real Indian giant squirrel's.

plates.name: Narmada Cave Bear
plates.why: Met on 15 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A massive, thick-furred cave bear climbing a cliff face toward a hanging honeycomb near the mouth of a high cave, absorbed and unhurried.

plates.name: Golden Honey-Goliath
plates.why: Met on 3 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A colossal golden bee, hand-sized, resting on the face of its huge comb hanging from a Narmada cliff, honey glistening in the cells.
plates.guess: Canon says colossal and never says how big. Hand-sized is my guess; paint it bigger if you picture it that way.

plates.name: Glacial Snow-Hare
plates.why: Met on 10 tiles only in Narmada.
plates.subject: A pure white, thick-furred hare with broad padded feet like snowshoes, sitting on snow at the foot of an ice wall.

plates.name: Indus Unicorn
plates.why: Met on 1 tiles only in Narmada.
plates.subject: A slender, swift, single-horned animal, bull-like in body, with one long horn rising from its brow as on the Harappan seals, standing at a river's edge.
plates.guess: Canon gives it one horn and swift feet. The body follows the Harappan seal animal, which is my inference.

plates.name: Garudasaur Eagle
plates.why: Met on 4 tiles in Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A colossal eagle with obsidian-black-tipped feathers, standing on its nest on a high volcanic ledge with its wings half open.

plates.name: Black-Striped Siege Bee
plates.why: Met on 15 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A giant bee with bold black stripes and ash-grey fuzz, resting on the rim of a honeycomb on a cliff with its wings folded.

plates.name: Sea Scorpion Queen
plates.why: Met on 140 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: An unsettlingly tall aquatic mimic. Its upper body resembles a serene, pale-skinned woman in a cowl of wet kelp, and below the waist it becomes an armoured, segmented dark-teal eurypterid tail flanked by jointed swimming paddles. It stands waist-deep and still in a southern lagoon at dusk, kelp moving around it.

plates.name: Vṛkṣaśmara
plates.why: Met on 40 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A massive, grey-mottled tree-mollusc descended from octopus after the extinction at the end of the Cretaceous. Its mantle is bulbous and weathered, like rough oak galls. It grips high branches with eight thick, muscular tentacles rimmed with keratinous suction discs, which fold flat against the bark when it rests. It rests high in a forest canopy, tentacles folded along a branch, half-hidden by leaves.

plates.name: Abyssal Storm-Watcher
plates.why: Met on 105 tiles in Lothal and Aravali.
plates.subject: A Cognitavi storm-watcher: an elegant, raven-sized bird with sleek, iridescent slate-grey plumage, a pronounced ivory casque above a sharp hooked beak, and luminous amber eyes marked with star-like pale flecks. It circles high over the open sea ahead of a monsoon squall, dark clouds building behind it.

plates.name: Vanga Pearl-Guide
plates.why: Met on 42 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A Cognitavi pearl-guide: an elegant, raven-sized bird with sleek, iridescent slate-grey plumage, a pronounced ivory casque above a sharp hooked beak, and luminous amber eyes marked with star-like pale flecks. It flies low in a patterned loop over calm sea above a pearl-oyster bank.

plates.name: Cognitavi
plates.why: Met on 19 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: An elegant, raven-sized bird with sleek, iridescent slate-grey plumage, a pronounced ivory casque above a sharp hooked beak, and luminous amber eyes marked with star-like pale flecks. It perches on a mooring post, head tilted, reading the water below.

plates.name: Cloud-Cricket
plates.why: Met on 35 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A lightweight orthopteran of the low-gravity heights, with a translucent pale-cyan exoskeleton, glass-like antennae and a slender, silver-veined abdomen that catches the light of the thin air. It sits on a tuft of moss at the rim of a floating island, open sky below.

plates.name: Mist-Valley Thrush
plates.why: Met on 22 tiles only in Aravali.
plates.subject: A plump songbird with soft ash-grey back feathers fading into a pale lavender-white breast speckled with tiny indigo chevrons. It sings from a bramble in a high, misty valley.

plates.name: Woolly Bactrian-Croc
plates.why: Met on 3 tiles only in Narmada.
plates.subject: A heavy, sprawling crocodyliform that survived in Asia into the age of mammals. Armoured moss-grey scales give way along the spine to a coat of thick, matted tawny fur, which frames two prominent fatty humps set just behind the heavy shoulder girdle. It walks a cold highland track, unhurried.

plates.name: Shrīmā
plates.why: Met on 17 tiles in Lothal, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: An amphibious, shrimp-like humanoid with a slender, translucent pale-amber shell of a body, draped in seaweed-silk and chains of cowrie shells, with two long, sweeping glass-like antennae that curve above its head like a living tiara. It stands in a shallow lagoon at dusk, swaying as though dancing.

plates.name: Quarry-Spawned Tendua
plates.why: Met on 4 tiles in Lothal, Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A heavy, wingless manticore of the ancient Permian simian-felid line, its stone-furred frame made of rough sandstone and river gravel. It has dexterous, ape-like forepaws, a segmented basalt scorpion tail, and a hauntingly expressive human face capable of subtle feeling and of mocking speech. It lies at rest against the wall of an old stone quarry, blending into the rock.

plates.name: Winged Behemoth Manticore
plates.why: Met on 3 tiles in Narmada and Aravali.
plates.subject: A colossal, shadowy manticore descended from corrupted sphinx-felids: the muscular body of a black leopard, flexible ape-like forelimbs, and broad membranous wings woven from brick-dust and shadow. Its strikingly expressive human face is crowned with scorpion-spine horns, and it can speak, in archaic dialects. It is perched on a ruined brick tower at dusk with its wings folded.

plates.name: Lunar-Reflection Wraith
plates.why: Met on 5 tiles in Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: An ethereal, faceless apparition made entirely of rippling silver light and the caustic patterns of moonlit water. It hovers a hand's breadth above the surface and mirrors, distorted, the silhouette of whoever looks into it. It hangs over the still water of a great stepped bath under a full moon.

plates.name: Clay-Born Watcher
plates.why: Met on 2 tiles in Lothal and Narmada.
plates.subject: A floating, palm-sized sphere of sun-baked Harappan terracotta around a single oversized, human-like eye of glazed obsidian that pulses with a faint golden light. It floats in the corner of a ruined Harappan courtyard.

plates.name: Ember-Scattering Sprite
plates.why: Met on 2 tiles in Lothal and Dwarka.
plates.subject: A tiny, crackling wisp of floating soot and bright orange sparks that darts through the air like a fiery dragonfly, leaving a short-lived trail of glowing ash. It darts above a campfire that has burned down to embers.

plates.name: Ember-Born Dancer
plates.why: Met on 1 tiles only in Narmada.
plates.subject: A tall, luminous figure woven from twisting golden flames and dark charcoal smoke, moving with fluid, hypnotic grace, as if performing a temple dance inside a bonfire. It dances in the heart of a tall bonfire at night.

plates.name: Scutosaurus Shield-Beast
plates.why: Met on 52 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A Permian pareiasaur: a massive, low, barrel-bodied herbivore covered in bony plates, often wearing weathered leather and brass harness from the work it is put to now. It stands placidly beside an old mossy earthwork, grazing, at peace.

plates.name: Scutosaurus Battering-Ram
plates.why: Met on 37 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A pareiasaur like the shield-beast, heavier in the head, with a broad bone-hard plate across its forehead, and a leather harness for hauling. It hauls a stone sledge along a terrace path, calm and steady.

plates.name: Gorgonopsid Pack-Leader
plates.why: Met on 48 tiles in Narmada, Dwarka and Aravali.
plates.subject: A large gorgonopsid: a sabre-toothed Permian synapsid, long-skulled and heavy-shouldered, larger than the rest of its line. It lies sphinx-like beside a basalt dolmen arch at twilight, eyes half closed, tail curled.

plates.name: Gorgonopsid War-Beast
plates.why: Met on 43 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A shaggy-haired, sabre-toothed gorgonopsid, heavy in the shoulder, often still wearing a harness from an older use. It rests tethered at the edge of a quiet campsite at twilight, dozing.

plates.name: Dimetrodon War-Mount
plates.why: Met on 34 tiles across all four maps.
plates.subject: A sail-backed synapsid whose sail is banded in the bright colours the Asura bred into its line, often saddled. Saddled and tethered near a peaceful camp, it basks with its sail turned to the sun.

plates.name: Rajasaurus Ambush-Drake
plates.why: Met on 5 tiles in Lothal and Narmada.
plates.subject: A colossal feathered abelisaurid with faint violet veins of Asura venom running through its scales. It sleeps coiled over a vine-draped temple archway, eyes closed, like a living stone gargoyle.

scenes.why: The most common take on high ground: stone, tin and copper off hills and mountains, about 850 times across the maps. It shows knapping today.
scenes.subject: Two hands breaking a block of dark basalt from a rocky hillside outcrop with a heavy hammerstone, fragments on the ground at the knees and a basket for the pieces, the land falling away to a valley behind.

scenes.why: Flint, clay and scar glass taken at the shore, 560 times. It shows knapping today.
scenes.subject: Two hands prising a nodule of flint out of pale beach shingle with a pointed stick, the tide line and moving surf just behind.

scenes.why: Cutting on the shore, 240 times: salt reed and mangrove poles. It shows reeds in a marsh today.
scenes.subject: Two hands cutting shoulder-high salt reeds at a brackish shore with a small blade, the sea's edge behind and a bundle already tied with twine.

scenes.why: Gathering under trees, 199 times: cardamom, ginger, long pepper. It shows reeds in a marsh today.
scenes.subject: Two hands picking green cardamom pods from low stems in forest shade, a small basket on the leaf litter, dappled light through the canopy.
Two hands scooping slick grey clay from a cut bank at the river's edge into a woven basket, the river moving past.

scenes.why: The sky islands are high but not climbed, so they are kept out of stoop-high: lodestone moss, prana pollen, aero bark.
scenes.subject: Seen from behind and close: a traveller kneeling at the grassy rim of a floating island, one hand steadying a pale boulder furred with silver-green moss, the other cutting a strip of it free with a small blade. Beyond the rim the ground simply ends: open cloud below, and other islands hanging small and blue in the far haze, trailing roots.

scenes.why: The most common bench work: 27 recipes carve something.
scenes.subject: Two hands carving a wooden bowl with a small bronze blade, the half-shaped bowl braced against a knee, pale curls of shavings falling onto a mat.

scenes.why: 14 recipes. Cooking plays as waiting for the right moment.
scenes.subject: Two hands lifting the lid of a clay pot on a small fire of three stones to look inside, steam rising, judging whether it is ready.
Two hands weaving a reed mat on the ground, the finished part flat under one knee, loose reeds fanned out ready.

scenes.why: 8 recipes. Firing plays as waiting for the right moment.
scenes.subject: Two hands lifting one turf from a small pit kiln of stacked pots banked with turf and dung, a warm glow inside, judging the moment to open it.
Two hands pushing a stone rubber across a saddle quern, grain turning to flour, a line of flour dust at the edge of the stone.
Two hands turning split fish on a drying rack in strong sun, one hand held flat above them to feel the heat.
Two hands with green-wood tongs pouring bright orange molten bronze from a small clay crucible into a stone mould set in sand.
Two hands leaning on a wooden lever press over a stack of crushed seed, oil running down a groove into a pot beneath.
Two hands spinning thread with a drop spindle, a hank of goat-hair fibre on one wrist, the spindle turning below.
Two hands working a stone scraper over a hide pegged out on the ground, a pot of dark bark liquor beside it.
Two hands stirring a wide-mouthed clay jar of fermenting mahua flowers with a stick, small bubbles on the surface, waiting for it to turn.
Two hands pouring a dark liquid slowly through layered cloth and charcoal into a clean pot, drop by drop.
Two hands lifting a soaked bundle of stems out of a shallow pool, fibre loosening from the rotting pith.
Two hands lashing a plank to the side of a half-built boat with fibre cord on a riverbank, a pot of pitch beside it.
Two hands working a skin bellows at the foot of a small clay furnace, thin smoke from its top, baskets of ore and charcoal beside it.

scenes.why: The night on open ground with only the bedroll. It shows the generic night today.
scenes.subject: Two hands spreading an oiled cloth bedroll on open ground at dusk, no fire, the grass still wet from rain, a notebook set on the pack.

scenes.why: Sitting the night out with nothing at all.
scenes.subject: Seen from behind: a traveller sitting up against a pack in the dark, knees drawn up, nothing to write by, a faint band of stars above.

lore.name: Vṛkṣaśmara
lore.note: Canon says it is grey, lives high in the canopy, is too large for a monkey, and files it as a mollusc. Nothing says what shape a tree-living mollusc that size is.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Cognitavi
lore.note: The navigator birds are clever and read water and weather, but canon never says their size, shape or plumage. The Vanga Pearl-Guide (42 tiles) and Abyssal Storm-Watcher (105 tiles) are both Cognitavi, so painting any one of them fixes the look of all three.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Cloud-Cricket
lore.note: Canon describes only its song in the thin air. Body and colour are missing.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Mist-Valley Thrush
lore.note: Canon gives its song and its food, not its plumage.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Woolly Bactrian-Croc
lore.note: A crocodile-mammal hybrid with two water-retention humps. How the humps sit on a crocodile's body, and whether it has fur or scales, are both open. The Sleek Dromedary-Croc and the Camelosuchus calf share the question.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Asura Thorn
lore.note: One of the most common plants in the game (567 tiles). Canon says hooked scrub planted as a living fence, and nothing about leaf, flower or colour.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Red Blood-Coral
lore.note: 631 tiles. The name gives the colour. Canon says it builds ridges and reclaims old aqueducts, but not what shape it grows in.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Healing Silver-root
lore.note: A medicinal tuber. Nothing says what the plant looks like above ground.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Bitter Marsh-root
lore.note: A root. Nothing says what the plant looks like above ground.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Lesser Whisper-Fig
lore.note: Canon says it whispers. Nothing visual beyond being a shrub-like fig on cliffs.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

lore.name: Blue Scholar's Moss
lore.note: It glows, which the art direction avoids. How bright, and what it looks like unlit, are open.
lore.settled: Described in canon's new `appearance` field, from the owner's notes of 29 September 2026.

rulings.name: Scutosaurus Shield-Beast
rulings.note: Bred by the Asura as living shields.
rulings.settled: Paint calm. Bred by the Asura tens of millions of years ago; now rare, tamed or feral, and no longer tied to them. Cards in the new batch.

rulings.name: Gorgonopsid Pack-Leader
rulings.note: Bred by Asura generals to lead war-packs.
